title: Implement insert (append and positional) with validation
description: Implement insert(value, index=None). No index appends to tail; index inserts at that position (0..len). Raise IndexError for negative or > len indexes without modifying the list; raise TypeError for non-int index (bool may be treated as invalid too). Add tests.
acceptance_criteria: insert at index 0, middle, and len produce correct order
Negative index and index > len raise IndexError and list unchanged
Inserting into an empty list at index 0 works
Tests for all of the above pass
spec_description: A Python module (linked_list.py) providing a singly linked list class `LinkedList` (with an internal `Node` class) that supports insert, delete, search, and reverse operations, plus a pytest test suite (test_linked_list.py) covering every method, including edge and error cases. Design decisions: values may be any Python object compared with ==; `insert(value, index=None)` appends to the tail when index is None, otherwise inserts before the given position (0 = head, len = tail); an out-of-range or non-integer index raises IndexError / TypeError respectively; `delete(value)` removes the first node whose value equals the argument and returns True, or returns False if not found (no exception); `search(value)` returns the zero-based index of the first match or -1 if absent; `reverse()` reverses the list in place and returns None. The class also supports len(), iteration, and `to_list()` to make behaviour testable.
